newsitem.title: INDIA: Software tops training at India's NIIT.
newsitem.headline: Software tops training at India's NIIT.

text.p: India's NIIT Ltd, a leading computer education company, said on Friday that revenue from software business surpassed revenue from training courses in 1995/96 (October-September).
"Software revenue this year is slightly beyond training revenue," managing director Rajendra Pawar told a news conference in New Delhi to discuss the company's annual results for 1995/96.

Powered by a growing market in multimedia and educational software, NIIT earned revenue of 1.45 billion rupees from its software product business in 1995/96, compared with 680 million rupees in 1994/95, NIIT president Vijay Thadani said.
Over the same period, revenue from training programmes and courses grew at a slower rate, rising to 1.38 billion rupees from 990 million rupees, he said.
"This year the basic growth thrust came from multimedia software products," Thadani said.

Total revenue from both sectors, which includes revenue accounted by 12 worldwide subsidiaries of NIIT, was 2.83 billion rupees in 1995/96. This is expected to grow to 4.0 billion rupees in 1996/97, Thadani said.

However, NIIT Ltd's net revenue of 2.28 billion rupees reported for 1995/96 did not take into account revenue from its global subsidiaries, as they have to be treated separately under Indian accounting law, company officials said.
In 1996/97, NIIT's net profit is expected to grow to 650 million rupees from 479 million rupees in the previous year, Thadani said.
NIIT expects to add 150 software titles during the year to the existing 64, he said.
Thadani said NIIT, aiming to become a major global player by 2000, planned to increase its strengths with the help of world-class facilities and development of branded products.
In 1995/96, the company added assets worth 460 million rupees, he said, adding that current expansion plans envisaged no rise in the company's equity base.
"We are looking at funding our growth through internal accruals and debt," Thadani said in a statement.
NIIT, formed in 1981, has subsidiaries in 12 countries including the United States, Britain, Sweden, France, Germany, Japan and Singapore.
NIIT has software factories in Delhi and Calcutta, and employs 2,700 people all over India. It trains more than 100,000 students ever year.
The company also has interests in providing software solutions, in which it has identified manufacturing, infrastructure, telecommunications and financial services as focus areas.
